claim_decisions.statement: The ex-post evaluation observed three of six hydromet stations: all three generated data, but two had partial functionality. Data were not centrally automated and farm advice was uneven.

pathways.climate_pressure: Seasonal water and pasture dependence in a dryland livestock system.
pathways.documented_impact: War left Tekezze–Setit watering areas inaccessible and concentrated herds around Goluj and reintegration sites.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict-related loss of transhumance/watering access and concentrated use of wells and cropland.
pathways.possible_consequence: Narrower seasonal coping options and localized livestock–farmer tensions were reported.
alternative_explanations: Borehole siting, herd numbers, settlement patterns and crop-residue management also shaped pressure.
pathways.uncertainty: Historical dryland coping mechanism from1999–2001 research, not measured climate-change impact, current violence or an evaluated adaptation project.
resilience_factors: Maintaining equitable water access and mobility options is relevant, without attributing pressures solely to displaced/returning people.
pathways.compact_statement: Near Goluj, border-war restrictions narrowed seasonal livestock water access and concentrated local resource pressures; findings are historical and exceptional.

gaps: Main directly checked the ex-post methods/hydromet findings and ODI Goluj passages. The reverse link concerns lost seasonal watering/mobility options, not a claim that climate caused the war.
AF-TERG's 2025 fieldwork visited selected sites and reports perceived/observed sustainability; GCA's solar-asset hazards are not household-loss estimates.

executive_assessment.text: Anseba's Habero/Hamelmalo water and agriculture evaluation adds concrete capacity and maintenance limits; older rainfall and solar-asset scenarios remain distinct.
Goluj illustrates historical war-related disruption of seasonal livestock water access, with localized resource tensions. This is not a current national climate-conflict trend.
